title: Cyclone Akvan forms in Bay; signal 2 hoisted at four seaports
excerpt: The Met Office raised distant warning signal 2 at Chattogram, Cox's Bazar, Mongla and Payra as Cyclone Akvan moves towards India's coast.

image.alt: Fishing trawlers pulled up on the beach at Cox's Bazar
image.credit: Tanvir Rahat / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0

content:
A depression in the Bay of Bengal has strengthened into Cyclone Akvan, and the Bangladesh Meteorological Department has asked the seaports of Chattogram, Cox's Bazar, Mongla and Payra to hoist distant warning signal No. 2, bdnews24 Bangla reported early on 17 November.

The storm may cross the coast of Andhra Pradesh in India on Friday evening as a very severe cyclone, according to a special bulletin from the department's Storm Warning Centre. Fishing boats and trawlers in the northern Bay were told to stay close to the coast and move with caution.

Maximum sustained winds within 54 km of the centre were 62 km per hour, rising to 88 km per hour in gusts. At 6pm on Monday the cyclone was 1,305 km south-west of Chattogram port, 1,245 km from Cox's Bazar, 1,225 km from Mongla and 1,205 km from Payra. Iran gave the storm its name, which means "demon".

Why it matters

The current track points away from Bangladesh, but cyclones in the Bay can change course, and outer bands can bring heavy rain and rough seas to the coast. Fishers lose income while boats stay ashore, and the Rohingya camps in Cox's Bazar, with their fragile shelters, are vulnerable to rain and wind. Disaster response NGOs and Cyclone Preparedness Programme volunteers will be watching the bulletins.

What to watch

Changes to the signal level and track in the Met Office's next bulletins, and any rain forecast for the coastal districts and Cox's Bazar.
